answer: Each new identity needs a sponsor, who locks 90 credits on the harbor registry for its voyage and pays a meadow fee: 20 for a first endorsement, 40 for a second, 80 for a third in one epoch. A fourth endorsement is rejected and burns the sponsor bond. A meadow board recomputes counts and burns all bonds of a sponsor tied to a proven fake, so a rented-sponsor ring loses its bonds. The k-th fake costs 90 bond plus a 20, 40, or 80 meadow fee by slot, 110 to 170 credits; 1,000 fakes need 334 sponsors and 136,640 credits. An honest identity needs one sponsor, one bond, and one 20-credit fee.
